newsitem.title: USA: Democrats gain slight edge in state legislatures.
newsitem.headline: Democrats gain slight edge in state legislatures.

text.p: Democrats took a slight edge in the battle for control of state legislative chambers, according to preliminary election results compiled Wednesday by National Conference of State Legislatures.
The conference reported that Democrats won the majority or at least a tie in six legislative chambers that had been controlled by Republicans going into Tuesday's election.

Preliminary election results indicated Democrats won control of the Connecticut Senate, Maine Senate, Tennessee Senate, Nevada Assembly and Vermont Senate. At least a tie with Republicans was reported in the Illinois and Michigan Houses.
Meanwhile, Republicans won the majority in the Florida House, Iowa Senate and Washington Senate from Democrats and both parties are tied in the Kentucky Senate, the conference reported.
Democrats managed to hold onto slim majorities in the Minnesota House, Missouri Senate, Texas Senate and Wisconsin Senate, the conference said.
In some states where Democrats were favored to pick up a chamber, Republicans held onto their control.
Those were the North Carolina House, Pennsylvania House and Wisconsin Assembly.
While Republicans still control the New York State Senate and Democrats still control the state Assembly, voters apparently pushed the Democrats into a few more seats in both chambers.
Before the election, Democrats controlled the Assembly 95 to 54, while Republicans controlled the Senate 37 to 24.
Election results are still being tallied, by reports give the Democrats a few more seats in each chmaber.
